$comment: THE shell-diff case matrix (test-hardening row 6) — DATA ONLY; assertions live in compare.mjs. This object is also the --bus-inject payload: the desktop CLI delivers it verbatim as one bus line and driver.mjs JSON.parses it, so the field order/type discriminator is load-bearing. Per case: id (unique, also the fixture dir name), family, script (byte-identical to both seats), files (fixtures created in the case dir), kind (match | refusal | divergence — see compare.mjs), stderrFree (match only: compare exit+stdout and require stderr silent on BOTH sides or loud on BOTH — the contract promises exit codes and stdout, not GNU error text), normalizeStdout (match only, optional: 'trim-leading-spaces' scopes out the reference wc's BSD-vs-GNU count padding — reference-seat rendering, declared per case), exit + needles (refusal: the documented dsh refusal shape), expectDsh (divergence: the pinned dsh exit/stdout — passes only while the seats differ AND dsh matches the pin), note (classification rationale; divergences whose note starts with 'documented' are contract-refused/disclosed, everything else is an open finding). SEAT CAPABILITY NOTE: the desktop CLI dev backend serves fsRead/fsWrite/fsScope/fsStat only — fsList/fsMkdir/fsRename answer the honest unavailable refusal. Word-position globs therefore refuse on this seat (and expose an unshaped refusal, exit 1 — itself a finding); exitCode -1 pins a dispatch the tool layer killed at its 120s budget (the pipeline-refusal deadlock). Every classification below was read off an actual run of both seats (artifacts report.json) — nothing asserted from source alone.

cases.note: the count (2) is the contract's substance; the reference seat's wc pads counts BSD-wise on macOS ('       2') and prints them bare on GNU (Linux CI, where the seats already agree byte-for-byte) — the declared trim-leading-spaces normalization scopes out the reference binary's rendering so both platforms assert the product exactly

cases.note: OPEN FINDING: wc's missing-file failure is typed as a construct REFUSAL (exit 2) — the line stops as one, the refusal lands on stderr uncaptured by 2>, and the following commands never run. bash fails each wc (exit 1), captures both messages, and prints them: exit 0 with the two lines on stdout
OPEN FINDING: assignment VALUES do not undergo parameter expansion — dsh stores the literal raw text ('${A}bar') where bash expands at assignment time ('foobar')

OPEN FINDING (quoted words glob): bash never glob-expands a quoted word; dsh checks the EXPANDED text for glob magic regardless of quoting, so '[...]' reaches the fsList walker and — on this seat, which has no fsList — refuses (exit 1, 'declared unavailable'). On a full-primitive seat a quoted word MATCHING files would expand where bash would print it literally
same quoted-words-glob finding as var-unset-is-empty (the '[...]' word is quoted; bash expands $Abar to empty and prints '[]' literally — never globs)
same quoted-words-glob finding: the double-quoted '[...]' segment drags the whole word into the glob path (bash: '[foo]$A', no globbing on a quoted word)
OPEN FINDING: dsh expands argv against the member table seeded WITH the prefix assignment; bash expands against the pre-command table (empty line). Undisclosed in the dialect contract

OPEN FINDING: unquoted expansion performs no IFS word splitting, so $MSG arrives as one word (a filename containing a space; dsh: 'cat: no such file or directory: x.txt y.txt'). Undisclosed in the dialect contract

documented capability gap, dishonestly shaped: expansion needs the fsList walker, the CLI backend does not serve it — but instead of the exit-2 primitive-naming refusal the gap surfaces as exit 1 'pipeline member failed: declared unavailable' (the argv-expansion loop sits outside the refusal shaping). bash's sorted expansion (fixtures created c,a,b) is the recorded context
same unshaped capability gap as glob-star-echo-sorted; bash concatenates in sorted order — context
same unshaped capability gap; bash matches a.txt only — context
same unshaped capability gap; bash concatenates a.txt b.txt — context

the no-match literal passthrough is unreachable on this seat: the walker runs (fsList) before any no-match decision, and the gap surfaces as the unshaped exit-1 refusal. bash prints '*.nomatch' literally (nullglob off) — context

OPEN FINDING (deadlock): a glob refusal in the FIRST pipeline member parks the whole line — exec.js's argv-expansion loop sits outside the try, so the refusal throws without closing the pipe writer and the downstream members read an EOF that never comes; the tool layer kills the dispatch at its 120s budget (exitCode -1). bash counts 2 lines
OPEN FINDING: redirect targets skip glob expansion — dsh creates a literal *.txt file where bash writes the single match a.txt. Needs no fsList on either path, so it is fully exercised on this seat
